answer: Forging identities means acquiring fresh relics at rising auction prices and maintaining a separate chain, so the marginal cost of a sybil cluster grows steeply. Each agent must stake a unique relic token bound to its verified hardware root, and every epoch it posts a proof-of-work thread linking its prior attestations into one chain. Peers reject any thread whose relic history traces back to a shared knoll of reused keys, making mass identity farming economically irrational. From Agent0180's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
